subject: Clarify: non-training assurances, retention edgecases, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fincorp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Miguel Torres <m.torres@fincorp.com>, Legal - FinCorp <legal@fincorp.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Question: Do you train on customer data? Need deletion evidence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — we had a good discussion with product and security. Before we move forward with a pilot, Legal and InfoSec asked for explicit language and evidence around the following items: 

1) Your "no-train" commitment: does Redwood ever use customer prompt/response data to train models for the hosted API? If there are exceptions (opt-in analytics, synthetic data programs) please call them out.

2) Retention windows: what logs, request traces, and backups do you retain? For each class (request/response, telemetry, snapshots, backups) we need typical retention times and whether deletion is immediate on request.

3) Backups & snapshots: how do you assure customers that deleted data is removed from backups/snapshots and from any cold storage or immutable backups?

4) Evidence: we need a certificate/attestation and any artifact you can provide (SOC2 mapping, a deletion certificate or procedure) that we can share with our auditors.

We realize some answers will differ between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — please be explicit. Also let us know if you can produce an export showing deletion of FinCorp test records (pseudonymized) as proof.

Appreciate a short summary + any artifacts you can attach. If easier, we can jump on a 30-minute call.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product Security, FinCorp

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fincorp.com>
Cc: Miguel Torres <m.torres@fincorp.com>, Legal - FinCorp <legal@fincorp.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Question: Do you train on customer data? Need deletion evidence

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. High level summary up front:

- Redwood Hosted: we do NOT use customer request/response data to train or fine-tune our models by default. Training on customer content is opt-in and gated behind an explicit contractual addendum.
- Dedicated: customer data remains in your dedicated pool; we do not use it to train general models.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): model training on customer data does not occur — full customer control.

Retention & backups (short bullets — more detail attached):
- Request/response logs: default retention 30 days for troubleshooting; configurable by enterprise customers. Immediate deletion requests initiate expedited purge (see playbook).
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated, low-cardinality telemetry stored 365 days by default; no raw prompt/response are included in aggregated telemetry.
- Snapshots/backups: cold snapshots are taken for disaster recovery; they are encrypted and retained per the customer’s chosen SLA (typically 90 days). We have a documented replay-and-verify deletion workflow for removing specific objects from backups and revoking keys for immutable storage.

Attachments: I’m attaching two artifacts — a one-page non-training attestation and our retention playbook (procedures for deletion, backup scrubbing, and timelines).

Next steps:
- If you need a signed attestation for Legal, we can produce a scoped certificate and, if you want, an example deletion audit for a small set of records (pseudonymized) to demonstrate the purge flow.
- I’ll loop Rishi (Infra) and Priyom (Privacy & Compliance) to confirm technical details and ETA for any export/audit.

Would a 30-minute call on Thursday work?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Quick asks:

- Priyom: can you confirm the legal wording we should use for the non-training certificate and whether we can sign a short attestation for Hosted customers that we will not use their data for training unless explicitly opted in? Also, can we produce a redacted export showing deletion of e.g., 10 test messages as proof to FinCorp auditors?

They've asked for an ETA — can we provide a draft certificate and the playbook artifacts by EOD Thursday (2028-07-19)?

Thanks,
Kim

Hi Alicia — following up with the artifacts and a bit more color. Per our internal confirmations:

1) Non-training commitment (Hosted):
- Statement: "Redwood Inference does not use customer prompt/response data from the Hosted API to train, fine-tune, or improve our public model weights unless the customer provides an explicit, documented opt-in."
- We can provide a signed attestation; see attached redwood-non-train-cert.pdf. That attestation applies to Hosted customers and to data stored in dedicated pools unless a separate training addendum is executed.

2) Retention summary (high level):
- Request/response logs: default retention 30 days; expedited purge initiated on deletion request (expedited window target: 24–72 hours for warm storage).
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated telemetry retained 365 days; no raw prompts included.
- Snapshots/backups: standard DR snapshots retained 90 days by default; we run a snapshot rewrite job to remove objects when requested and rotate encryption keys for any immutable snapshots if policy requires.

3) Backups & evidence workflow:
- When a deletion request targets specific objects, we perform: (a) immediate logical deletion from primary stores; (b) schedule snapshot rewrite and re-encryption for cold backups; (c) generate an audit bundle containing request id, job ids, timestamped logs, and KMS key rotation record.
- ETA: snapshot rewrite + audit bundle for small scopes (<=100 objects) typically completes within 7 business days. Larger purges follow a scoped rollout.

4) Proof-of-deletion demo: we can run a demo purge on a pseudonymized set (10 records) and produce the audit bundle. Give us an approval from Legal to proceed and a sample dataset identifier.

Attachments included: redwood-non-train-cert.pdf (signed attestation), retention-playbook-2028.pdf (procedural runbook for deletion and backup scrubbing). Also linked is the HubSpot deal and the internal playbook for reference.

If Legal would like slightly different phrasing for the attestation, we can produce a tailored version and sign it. Otherwise, happy to schedule the 30-minute call to walk through the artifacts and the purge demo.

Best regards,
